short: RORA, RORB and RORC (RORalpha/beta/gamma) are nuclear receptors that bind DNA as monomers to the ROR response element, or RORE: an AGGTCA nuclear-receptor half-site preceded by a 5-6 bp AT-rich extension, most often written AAAGTAGGTCA. The extension is read by a C-terminal extension of the DNA-binding domain lying in the minor groove, and it is the only feature that distinguishes a RORE from the half-site shared by many other nuclear receptors. ROREs form the second transcriptional loop of the mammalian circadian clock, where RORs activate Bmal1 in competition with the REV-ERB repressors at the same sites. RORgammat, a thymus-restricted RORC isoform, drives the Th17 program and is a drug target in autoimmune disease.
long:
## The factors

The ROR (RAR-related orphan receptor) group is encoded by three human genes: *RORA* (NR1F1, RORalpha), *RORB* (NR1F2, RORbeta) and *RORC* (NR1F3, RORgamma; the symbol *RORG* is used for it in HOCOMOCO and in the Vierstra archetypes). Each protein has the standard nuclear-receptor layout — an N-terminal A/B region, a DNA-binding domain (DBD) built from two zinc-coordinating modules, a hinge, and a ligand-binding domain (LBD) ending in an AF-2 helix. Unlike the steroid and RXR-partnered receptors, RORs bind DNA as monomers, using a C-terminal extension (CTE) of the DBD in addition to the zinc modules. Alternative promoters and splicing generate isoforms with different N-termini (RORalpha1-4; RORgamma and the thymus-restricted RORgammat), and these N-termini change DNA-binding behavior rather than just transactivation. Expression differs sharply: *RORA* is broad (cerebellum, liver, many tissues), *RORB* is largely restricted to retina, pineal gland and specific brain regions, and *RORC* is expressed in liver, muscle and skeletal tissue, with RORgammat confined to thymocytes and to T-helper and innate lymphoid subsets. RORalpha and RORgamma are constitutively active in reporter assays, with cholesterol and oxysterol derivatives occupying the LBD pocket.

## The motif

The ROR response element (RORE) is a single nuclear-receptor half-site with a 5' extension, conventionally written as an AT-rich stretch of 5-6 bp followed by RGGTCA. The canonical monomeric site established for RORalpha1 is often quoted as the 11-mer AAAGTAGGTCA; the motif models in this family converge on a slightly shorter 10-mer, A(A/T)NTAGGTCA (the pooled data consensus here is AAbTAGGTCA). Both renderings describe the same element — the discrepancy is only how many of the weakly constrained AT positions a given model retains.

Structurally, the split is clean. The zinc modules place a recognition helix in the major groove of AGGTCA, which supplies most of the information content; the CTE (the A-box/T-box region) lies along the minor groove of the AT-rich 5' extension and is what converts a generic half-site into a RORE. The crystal structure of the closely related REV-ERBalpha DBD plus CTE on a direct repeat, and the structure of the monomeric receptor NGFI-B, both show this arrangement directly. Without the 5' extension the motif is just the half-site shared by dozens of nuclear receptors.

RORs also bind extended sites: HT-SELEX models in this family include ~18-bp tandem arrangements (AAGTAGGTCAGTAGGTCA), i.e. two half-sites in direct repeat with a 2-bp gap. All eleven motifs assigned here collapse onto the same core (family cohesion 0.87), and none is flagged as mislabelled. RORA, RORB and RORC are not distinguishable from sequence.

## Where it acts

ROREs sit in promoters and enhancers, not preferentially in CpG islands. The best-characterized examples are the two ROREs in the *Bmal1* (*ARNTL*) promoter, with further sites at *Cry1*, *Npas2* and *Nfil3*. In immune cells, RORgammat acts through ROREs in the *IL17A*/*IL17F* locus and its conserved non-coding regions, alongside RUNX1, BATF and IRF4. In the circadian cis-regulatory grammar, the RORE is one of three elements — E-box (CLOCK:BMAL1), D-box, and RORE — whose combination sets the phase of a rhythmic promoter; the RORE contributes the late-night/early-morning component. Because the informative part is a 10-mer with several degenerate positions, matches are common: expect on the order of 10^5 hits genome-wide at permissive thresholds, so genomic occurrence alone carries little weight.

## Biology and disease

The *staggerer* mouse, a spontaneous *Rora* deletion, loses cerebellar Purkinje cells and is ataxic, and RNAi and mutant analyses place Rora in the mammalian clock, where loss shortens or destabilizes period. *Rorb* is required for photoreceptor and pineal gene programs. *Rorc*-null mice lack lymph nodes and Peyer's patches and show increased thymocyte apoptosis, and RORgammat is required for the Th17 program, making it a drug target in psoriasis and other autoimmune disease; RORgamma inverse agonists and RORalpha/gamma agonists have both been pursued clinically.

## Reading a hit

A RORE match identifies the family, not the member: nothing in the sequence separates RORA from RORB from RORC. More importantly, it does not separate ROR from REV-ERB. NR1D1 and NR1D2 bind the same RORE and the same 2-bp-spaced direct repeat, and the Vierstra archetype AC0123:NR1D/RORC states this by naming both groups. The two are told apart by tissue, circadian phase and cofactor (coactivator versus NCoR-HDAC3), not by motif.

Second, check that your hit includes the AT-rich extension. A bare AGGTCA is shared with ESRRA, NR5A, NR4A and the RXR heterodimer partners; scanning with the full 10-11-mer is the only way to make the call specific. Third, weigh the evidence code. RORB.H14CORE.0.SM.B rests on in vitro selection (HT-SELEX plus methyl-HT-SELEX) and supports a direct binding claim; RORA.H14CORE.0.P.C is ChIP-only at grade C and its consensus drifts at the 3' end. Finally, ChIP-derived versions of this motif can be contaminated by indirect binding: in mouse liver, most REV-ERBalpha ChIP peaks reflect tethering to HNF6 rather than direct RORE occupancy, and the same mechanism is available to RORs.
caveats: Treat a RORE hit as a family-level call, and remember the family boundary is porous: REV-ERB (NR1D1/NR1D2) binds the same element, so a match is really a 'ROR/REV-ERB site' unless expression or phase data break the tie. RORA, RORB and RORC are not separable from sequence — all eleven motifs here collapse onto one core. Matches to the bare AGGTCA half-site are not ROREs; require the AT-rich 5' extension. Prefer the in vitro-derived models (HOCOMOCO evidence S/M, e.g. RORB.H14CORE.0.SM.B) over ChIP-only entries such as RORA.H14CORE.0.P.C, which is grade C. The 10-mer is common enough that occurrence alone is weak evidence.
